claims.statement: Dallas City Council approved AI-enabled cameras for brush and bulky trash collection trucks.
claims.text: Dallas City Council approved AI-enabled cameras for brush and bulky trash collection trucks.
claims.quote: The Dallas City Council has approved the deployment of artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled cameras on brush and bulky trash collection trucks
claims.scope_note: The December 2025 approval does not alone establish the later live deployment date.

claims.statement: The city's brush-truck cameras take side-facing still photos of the curb line from the public right-of-way as trucks travel their normal routes.
claims.text: The city's brush-truck cameras take side-facing still photos of the curb line from the public right-of-way as trucks travel their normal routes.
claims.quote: As brush trucks run their normal routes, side-mounted cameras will periodically take still photos of the curb line visible from the public right-of-way.
claims.value_text: side-mounted still photos from the public right-of-way
claims.scope_note: The source describes periodic still capture, not continuous video or camera zoom.

claims.statement: Dallas says computer vision analyzes those images for visible conditions such as debris piles, illegal dumping, and bulk trash participation.
claims.text: Dallas says computer vision analyzes those images for visible conditions such as debris piles, illegal dumping, and bulk trash participation.
claims.quote: The images will be analyzed using computer vision technology to identify visible conditions such as debris piles, illegal dumping, and bulk trash participation, all from the public right-of-way.
claims.value_text: computer vision flags visible property conditions
claims.scope_note: A flag is a potential condition, not a proven violation or automatic citation.

claims.statement: Dallas's official camera briefing says there is a human in the loop for all actions and describes the system as not automated ticketing.
claims.text: Dallas's official camera briefing says there is a human in the loop for all actions and describes the system as not automated ticketing.
claims.quote:
NOT automated ticketing
➢There is a human in the loop
for all actions
claims.value_text: human in the loop for all actions
claims.scope_note: This states the city's workflow policy; it is not an independent audit of each notice.

claims.statement: FOX 4 reports that a September 8 city memo says citations follow an in-person code-officer inspection and notice to the property owner.
claims.text: FOX 4 reports that a September 8 city memo says citations follow an in-person code-officer inspection and notice to the property owner.
claims.quote: The memo also states citations are only issued after a code officer inspects the property in-person and provides notice to the owner.
claims.scope_note: The September 8 memo was not directly retrieved; this is FOX's account of its contents. Do not extend the in-person requirement to courtesy notices.

claims.statement: NBC 5 reports the city said it sent courtesy notices to 3,700 property owners after camera detections.
claims.text: NBC 5 reports the city said it sent courtesy notices to 3,700 property owners after camera detections.
claims.quote: the city said it has also sent what it calls "courtesy notices" to 3,700 property owners, notifying them of detected violations.
claims.scope_note: The notice total is city-reported through NBC, not independently counted. The city calls these courtesy notices; their wording requests correction.

claims.statement: NBC 5 quotes the city manager's memo as saying 57 citations were issued at 34 properties for non-compliance.
claims.text: NBC 5 quotes the city manager's memo as saying 57 citations were issued at 34 properties for non-compliance.
claims.quote: 57 citations have been issued at 34 properties for non-compliance
claims.scope_note: This is a memo figure quoted by NBC and corroborated by FOX, not a directly inspected September 8 memo. It does not establish that AI issued citations automatically.

claims.statement: NBC 5 reports that Oak Cliff homeowner Sarrah Morrison received a camera-photo notice alleging litter and a roof condition on her property.
claims.text: NBC 5 reports that Oak Cliff homeowner Sarrah Morrison received a camera-photo notice alleging litter and a roof condition on her property.
claims.quote:
But that's not how Sarrah Morrison took it when a notice arrived in her Oak Cliff mailbox.

It said there were violations on her property, including “litter” and a roof that was "not in operating condition." The notice came with a photo that the AI cameras snapped of her house.
claims.value_text: Morrison received notice with camera image
claims.scope_note: The article identifies Morrison in Oak Cliff. The roof condition is an allegation in the notice, not a verified defect.

claims.statement: NBC 5 says Morrison disputed the roof flag and supplied documentation describing permanent flashing installed years earlier.
claims.text: NBC 5 says Morrison disputed the roof flag and supplied documentation describing permanent flashing installed years earlier.
claims.quote: She provided documentation showing it's a permanent piece of flashing installed years ago to protect an area of the flat roof.
claims.scope_note: NBC reports the documentation but this validator did not inspect the document. Do not claim the city formally cleared the flag.

claims.statement: Morrison told NBC 5 that the notice frightened her and led her to clean her yard in 100-degree heat despite a medical condition.
claims.text: Morrison told NBC 5 that the notice frightened her and led her to clean her yard in 100-degree heat despite a medical condition.
claims.quote: Morrison said the notice panicked her so much that, despite a medical condition, she spent time cleaning her yard in 100-degree heat.
claims.value_text: Morrison reports cleaning yard in 100-degree heat
claims.scope_note: NBC attributes the experience to Morrison. The article does not show that she received a citation.

claims.statement: NBC 5 reports that Morrison's letter asked her to correct alleged violations to avoid later enforcement.
claims.text: NBC 5 reports that Morrison's letter asked her to correct alleged violations to avoid later enforcement.
claims.quote: Please correct the violations promptly to avoid further enforcement action.
claims.value_text: courtesy notice asks correction to avoid enforcement
claims.scope_note: The quoted sentence verifies the request. The same NBC article separately quotes the courtesy-notice disclaimer. The city says it is not a formal warning or citation.

claims.statement: FOX 4 reported a city-manager briefing on the cameras was planned for October 19, 2026.
claims.text: FOX 4 reported a city-manager briefing on the cameras was planned for October 19, 2026.
claims.quote: A briefing on the cameras from Dallas City Manager Kim Tolbert will take place on October 19.
claims.scope_note: The schedule is reported by FOX; no official meeting notice was found in this validation pass. Do not claim it occurred or that its date is guaranteed.

rejected.claim: AI automatically issues tickets or sends citations without a person
rejected.reason: The city's primary briefing says this is not automated ticketing and says a human participates in all actions. FOX reports an in-person inspection before a citation.

rejected.claim: Every courtesy notice was preceded by an in-person property inspection
rejected.reason: The in-person requirement in FOX's account of the memo concerns citations. The sources do not establish an inspection before each courtesy notice.

rejected.claim: The city directly verified 3,700 notices and 57 citations in a retrieved September 8 memo
rejected.reason: The September 8 memo was not directly retrieved. NBC and FOX report its figures; claims keep that attribution.

rejected.claim: Morrison's roof was in violation or she received a citation
rejected.reason: Her alleged roof defect was disputed with documentation; NBC describes a courtesy notice and does not report her receiving a citation.

rejected.claim: The October 19 briefing is confirmed on a current official agenda
rejected.reason: Only FOX's September 18 report of the planned briefing was verified; no current official notice was obtained.

rejected.claim: Ten thousand properties were scanned as a current program total
rejected.reason: FOX attributes 10,000 to a September 8 memo, while NBC reports 21,000 addresses with potential violations over four months. The units and periods differ, and a direct memo was unavailable.
